title: A quasi-coherent algebra on a qcqs scheme is the directed colimit of its finite type quasi-coherent subalgebras (Stacks 05JT)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. A *quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra* is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras whose underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra. A *quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-subalgebra* of $\mathcal A$ is a subsheaf $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal A$ such that $\mathcal B(U)$ is an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-subalgebra of $\mathcal A(U)$ for every open $U$ and whose underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent; it is *of finite type* if for every affine open $U\subseteq X$ the $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra $\mathcal B(U)$ is finitely generated. Let $\Sigma$ be the set of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-subalgebras of finite type of $\mathcal A$, ordered by inclusion. Then (a) $\Sigma$ is a directed set (nonempty, and any two members are contained in a third); (b) the inclusions $\mathcal B\hookrightarrow\mathcal A$ ($\mathcal B\in\Sigma$) induce an isomorphism $\varinjlim_{\mathcal B\in\Sigma}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal A$, the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] taken in the category of sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras; (c) in particular, for every affine open $U\subseteq X$ every element of $\mathcal A(U)$ lies in $\mathcal B(U)$ for some $\mathcal B\in\Sigma$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-directed-colimit-finite-presentation] to the underlying quasi-coherent module of $\mathcal A$; $X$ is qcqs. It gives a nonempty directed system of finitely presented modules $\mathcal F_i$ with colimit maps $\varphi_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-images-module-colimit] to this system. The images $\mathcal C_i=\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F_i)\to\mathcal A)$ belong to $\Sigma$, and every affine section of $\mathcal A$ lies in one of them. This proves (c).

proof.text: $\Sigma$ is a set of subsheaves of $\mathcal A$, partially ordered by inclusion. Step 2 supplies a member, even when $X$ is empty, since $I$ is nonempty. Step 1 supplies upper bounds for pairs. Thus $\Sigma$ is a directed set, proving (a).

proof.text: Form the cocone c with vertex A and legs the subobject arrows. For each affine open U, all legs on sections are injective (a mono in Under remains mono in ring sheaves and in presheaves, and ring monos are injective). Step 2 makes them jointly surjective. Apply Mathlib Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf' to the underlying types: two sections at one stage with the same image are already equal. Its universal map to any compatible ring cocone preserves 0 and 1 by using any stage; for addition and multiplication, represent both inputs and move them to a common upper stage from Step 1. The stage maps preserve the operations, so the universal map does also. This proves the ring-colimit property on U directly from [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], without using a separate colimit-existence theorem or shrinking the subobject index. For a cocone t in algebra sheaves, let alpha_U be these ring universal maps. Precomposition with every inclusion and the ring-colimit factorization equations reduce their naturality to the naturality of the legs of t. Affine opens are a basis by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; extend alpha to a ring-sheaf map g by restrictHomEquivHom in [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis]. Choose any subalgebra B using Step 3. On affine U, O(U) -> A(U) factors through B(U), and alpha_U composed with B(U) -> A(U) is the leg t_B,U. The algebra-map condition for t_B therefore proves that g respects O_X; basis hom_ext extends this equation globally. The extension equation and the affine factorization equations show inclusion_B composed with g is t_B. Any other algebra map with these equations equals g on every affine by ring-colimit uniqueness, hence globally by basis hom_ext. Thus c is a colimit in all commutative algebra sheaves, proving (b).
